title: Real conversation
goal: Tell a friend what happened, react while they tell you their news, pass on what people said and keep a chat going.
intro:
This last unit of Part 1 is about the thing you have been working towards: **real conversation**. You'll learn how Telugu speakers tell a friend what happened (**అసలు ఏం జరిగిందంటే...** 'so what actually happened was...'), how listeners react (**నిజంగానా?**, **బాబోయ్!**, **హమ్మయ్య!**), and the little words that keep a chat moving: **అంటే** (I mean), **మరి** (so, and what about), **కదా** (right?), **అన్నట్టు** (by the way), **ఇంతకీ** (so anyway).

Two structures let you build longer sentences: **relative clauses** (*నిన్న నేను కలిసిన అమ్మాయి*, 'the girl I met yesterday') and **reported speech** with **అని** (*వస్తా అన్నాడు*, 'he said he'd come'). You'll also start hearing the short spoken verb forms friends use: *వెళ్ళా* for *వెళ్ళాను*, *చెప్తా* for *చెప్తాను*.

vocab.note: ఏంటి సంగతి? = what's up? · plural సంగతులు
విషయం ఏంటంటే... = the thing is... · పెద్ద విషయం కాదు = it's no big deal
అదో పెద్ద కథ = it's a long story
గొడవ పడు = to fight, quarrel · గొడవ చేయు = to make a fuss
English loan · జోక్ చేయు = to joke, kid · జోకులు వేయు = to crack jokes
అబద్ధం చెప్పు = to tell a lie · అబద్ధాలు = lies
నా మాట విను = listen to me · మాట ఇచ్చాను = I gave my word
past అన్నాను (spoken అన్నా), అన్నాడు, అంది, అన్నారు · non-past అంటాను, అంటాడు, అంటుంది · didn't say: అనలేదు
after the oblique form: నీ గురించి (about you), దాని గురించి (about it), సినిమా గురించి

vocab.en: I mean, that is; so you mean...
vocab.note: Literally 'if one says'. Also introduces an explanation: ఏం జరిగిందంటే... (what happened is...)
మరి నువ్వు? = and you? · మరి ఇప్పుడు? = so now what?

vocab.en: actually, really; (with a negative) at all
vocab.note: అసలు రాలేదు = didn't come at all · stronger: అస్సలు

vocab.en: in fact, actually, to be honest

vocab.note: నిజంగా? = really? · నిజంగానా? = seriously?
After a question word + -ఓ: వస్తాడో రాడో ఏమో = who knows if he'll come or not
Asks for agreement or reminds: నువ్వు వస్తావు కదా? = you're coming, right?
Opens a new topic you've just remembered: అన్నట్టు, రవి ఫోన్ చేశాడా?

vocab.en: so anyway, so (getting to the point)
vocab.note: Brings the chat back to the main question: ఇంతకీ ఏమైంది? = so what happened in the end?

vocab.en: in the end, all in all; finally (after some trouble)
well then, how about...; never mind
vocab.note: పోనీ, రేపు? = how about tomorrow then? · పోనీలే = never mind, let it go
For shock or fear; stronger: అయ్యబాబోయ్!
Surprise, or calling a friend's attention
నీకేమైనా పిచ్చా? = are you crazy? · పిచ్చోడు = crazy guy (often affectionate between friends)

phrases.en: Don't try to fool me! (lit. don't put a flower in my ear)
Where was I? (lit. up to where did I tell?)
phrases.note: దాకా is the everyday word for వరకు (up to)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: the girl I met, the bus that goes
grammar.body:
Telugu has no words for 'who / which / that'. Instead the verb turns into an **adjective-like participle** and goes **before** the noun, with everything that belongs to it in front:
• past **-ఇన** (-ina): *వచ్చిన అబ్బాయి* (the boy who came), *నేను కలిసిన అమ్మాయి* (the girl I met), *నువ్వు చెప్పిన హోటల్* (the place you told me about)
• non-past **-ఏ** (-ē): *వెళ్ళే బస్సు* (the bus that goes / will go), *తెలుగు మాట్లాడే ఫ్రెండ్స్* (friends who speak Telugu)
• negative **-అని** (-ani): *రాని వాళ్ళు* (those who don't / didn't come)

To say **'the one who / the thing that'**, add **-వాడు** (man), **-ది** (woman or thing) or **-వాళ్ళు** (people) to the participle: *వచ్చినవాడు* (the guy who came), *నువ్వు అన్నది* (what you said), *నేను చెప్పేది* (what I'm saying).

The trap: English puts the clause after the noun ('the girl *I met yesterday*'); Telugu puts it before, and the clause's verb takes the participle form, not a normal ending: say *నిన్న కలిసిన అమ్మాయి*, not *అమ్మాయి నిన్న కలిశాను*.

examples.native: పార్టీలో మనం కలిసిన అమ్మాయి పేరు ఏంటి?
examples.roman: pārṭīlō manam kalisina ammāyi pēru ēṇṭi?
examples.en: What's the name of the girl we met at the party?

examples.native: నువ్వు చెప్పిన సినిమా చూశాను, సూపర్‌గా ఉంది.
examples.roman: nuvvu cheppina sinimā chūshānu, sūpargā undi.
examples.en: I watched the film you told me about, it was great.
Is this the bus that goes to Koti?

examples.native: తెలుగు మాట్లాడే ఫ్రెండ్స్ ఉంటే తొందరగా నేర్చుకుంటావు.
examples.roman: telugu māṭlāḍē phreṇḍs uṇṭē tondaragā nērchukuṇṭāvu.
examples.en: If you have friends who speak Telugu, you'll learn fast.

grammar.title: Reported speech: అని, -మని and -అట
grammar.body:
Telugu keeps the speaker's **own words** and closes them with **అని**, then adds a verb of saying: *ఐదు నిమిషాల్లో వస్తా అని అన్నాడు* = he said 'I'll come in five minutes' = he said he'd come in five minutes. Notice that the quoted verb stays in the first person (*వస్తా*, I'll come). Questions are reported the same way with **అడుగు** (ask): *ఎక్కడ ఉన్నావు అని అడిగింది* (she asked where you were).

In speech **అని + అను** usually fuse: *వస్తా అని అన్నాడు* → *వస్తానన్నాడు* (vastānannāḍu); after a verb in -ఆ just *వస్తా అన్నాడు*.

**Reported commands** use **-మని** on the verb stem: *రమ్మని చెప్పింది* (she told [me] to come), *తీసుకోమని చెప్పారు* (they told [me] to take it). Fused: *రమ్మంది*, *వెళ్ళమన్నాడు*.

**Hearsay**, 'apparently / I heard that', is **-అట** (-aṭa) on the verb: *పెళ్ళైందట* (apparently [she] got married), *రారట* (apparently they're not coming). It's the gossip ending.

examples.en: He said he'd be here in five minutes.

examples.native: నువ్వు ఎక్కడ ఉన్నావు అని అమ్మ అడిగింది.
examples.roman: nuvvu ekkaḍa unnāvu ani amma aḍigindi.

examples.en: They told me to come early.
What did he say? He said 'nothing'.

grammar.title: Telling it and reacting: story words, fillers, reactions
grammar.body:
**Telling a story.** Start with **అసలు ఏం జరిగిందంటే...** or **విషయం ఏంటంటే...** ('the thing is...'): *-అంటే* after a question turns it into an introduction. Then string events together with **మొదట** (first), **ఆ తర్వాత** (after that), **ఇంతలో** (just then), **చివరికి** (in the end) and **మొత్తానికి** (in the end, after all that).

**Spoken verb forms.** In chat with friends the final **-ను** of 'I' forms drops: *వెళ్ళాను → వెళ్ళా*, *చెప్తాను → చెప్తా*, *ఉన్నాను → ఉన్నా*. Use the full form when writing or speaking politely.

**Keeping the chat going.** **అంటే** (I mean / so you mean) · **మరి** (so, and what about) · **అసలు** (actually; with a negative 'at all') · **కదా** (right?) · **అన్నట్టు** (by the way) · **ఇంతకీ** (so anyway) · **ఏదేమైనా** (anyway) · **పోనీ** (how about / never mind).

**Reacting.** A Telugu listener is never silent: **ఊ** (mm), **అవునా?** (oh yeah?), **నిజంగానా?** (seriously?), **తర్వాత?** (and then?), **అబ్బా!** (wow / ugh), **బాబోయ్!** (yikes), **అయ్యో, పాపం** (oh no, poor thing), **హమ్మయ్య!** (phew).

examples.native: అసలు విషయం ఏంటంటే, నాకు ఉద్యోగం దొరికింది!
examples.roman: asalu viṣayam ēṇṭaṇṭē, nāku udyōgam dorikindi!
examples.en: The real news is, I got the job!
By the way, did Ravi call?

examples.native: మొదట భయపడ్డా, కానీ మొత్తానికి బాగానే జరిగింది.
examples.roman: modaṭa bhayapaḍḍā, kānī mottāniki bāgānē jarigindi.
examples.en: I was scared at first, but all in all it went fine.

dialogue.title: The interview story
dialogue.setting: Hyderabad. Kiran meets his friend Sravani for Irani chai the day after her job interview.

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.native: ఏంటి శ్రావణి, ఏంటి సంగతి? నిన్న ఇంటర్వ్యూ ఎలా జరిగింది?
lines.roman: ēṇṭi shrāvaṇi, ēṇṭi saṅgati? ninna inṭarvyū elā jarigindi?
lines.en: Hey Sravani, what's up? How did yesterday's interview go?

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.en: Go on, tell me, what happened?

lines.speaker: Sravani
lines.native: అసలు ఏం జరిగిందంటే, ఉదయం మెట్రోలో సీటు కోసం ఒక ఆవిడతో గొడవ పడ్డా.
lines.roman: asalu ēm jarigindaṇṭē, udayam meṭrōlō sīṭu kōsam oka āviḍatō goḍava paḍḍā.
lines.en: So what actually happened is, in the morning I had a row with a lady on the metro over a seat.

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.en: You? A row? Are you kidding?

lines.speaker: Sravani
lines.native: నిజంగా! ఆవిడ నా సీటులో బ్యాగ్ పెట్టింది. తీయమని చెప్పా, తీయను అంది.
lines.roman: nijaṅgā! āviḍa nā sīṭulō byāg peṭṭindi. tīyamani cheppā, tīyanu andi.
lines.en: Really! She'd put her bag on my seat. I told her to move it, she said she wouldn't.

lines.speaker: Sravani
lines.native: ఇంటర్వ్యూకి వెళ్ళా. లోపల కూర్చున్న మేడం ఎవరో తెలుసా? మెట్రోలో నేను గొడవ పడిన ఆవిడే!
lines.roman: inṭarvyūki veḷḷā. lōpala kūrchunna mēḍam evarō telusā? meṭrōlō nēnu goḍava paḍina āviḍē!
lines.en: I went in for the interview. Guess who the woman sitting inside was? The very lady I fought with on the metro!

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.en: Oh my god! You're pulling my leg!

lines.speaker: Sravani
lines.native: ఒట్టు! మొదట నాకు చాలా భయం వేసింది. కానీ ఆవిడ నవ్వి, మీకు ధైర్యం ఎక్కువే అంది.
lines.roman: oṭṭu! modaṭa nāku chālā bhayam vēsindi. kānī āviḍa navvi, mīku dhairyam ekkuvē andi.
lines.en: I swear! At first I was really scared. But she laughed and said, 'You've certainly got nerve.'

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.en: So anyway, did you get the job or not?

lines.speaker: Sravani
lines.native: వచ్చింది! ఆ మెట్రో ఆవిడే ఇప్పుడు నా బాస్!
lines.roman: vachchindi! ā meṭrō āviḍē ippuḍu nā bās!
lines.en: I got it! That metro lady is now my boss!

lines.speaker: Kiran
lines.native: అరే, సూపర్! అయితే ఈరోజు ఇరానీ చాయ్ నీ ట్రీట్!
lines.roman: arē, sūpar! ayitē īrōju irānī chāy nī ṭrīṭ!
lines.en: Hey, awesome! Then today's Irani chai is your treat!

culture: A Telugu listener keeps up a running commentary: *ఊ*, *అవునా?*, *అబ్బా!*, *తర్వాత?*. Silence while someone tells you their news can sound cold, so react out loud. With friends people drop the final *-ను* (*వెళ్ళా*, *చెప్తా*) and call each other *రా* (to a man) or *ఏ / వే* (to a woman): *చెప్పరా!*, *ఏంటే?*. Young men in Andhra and Telangana also call close friends *బావా* ('brother-in-law') or *మామా* ('uncle'), entirely affectionately. Regional colour is strong: in Telangana and much of Hyderabad you'll hear *ఏంది?* for *ఏంటి?* and *ఎట్లా* for *ఎలా*, with Hindi-Urdu words mixed in; Coastal Andhra speech is closer to the standard taught here. English words slip in everywhere (*సూపర్*, *టెన్షన్*, *సీన్*), and swearing an oath is *ఒట్టు!* ('I swear!'). Proverbs (*సామెతలు*) are still loved, but among friends you're more likely to hear a film dialogue quoted than a proverb.

tip.title: Story words, and the spoken -ఆ
tip.body:
- Open with **అసలు ఏం జరిగిందంటే...** or **విషయం ఏంటంటే...** (the thing is...).
- Then: **మొదట** first · **ఇంతలో** just then · **చివరికి** / **మొత్తానికి** in the end.
- With friends the 'I' ending **-ను** drops: వెళ్ళాను → **వెళ్ళా**, చెప్తాను → **చెప్తా**.

sentences.native: ఏంటి సంగతి? చాలా రోజుల తర్వాత కనిపించావు!
sentences.roman: ēṇṭi saṅgati? chālā rōjula tarvāta kanipinchāvu!
sentences.en: What's up? Haven't seen you in ages!

sentences.native: మొదట నేను బస్సు ఎక్కా, తర్వాత ఆటో తీసుకున్నా.
sentences.roman: modaṭa nēnu bassu ekkā, tarvāta āṭō tīsukunnā.
sentences.en: First I took the bus, then I got an auto.
Just then it started to rain.

sentences.native: చివరికి రాత్రి పది గంటలకి ఇంటికి చేరా.
sentences.roman: chivariki rātri padi gaṇṭalaki iṇṭiki chērā.
sentences.en: In the end I got home at ten at night.
We got the tickets in the end!

sentences.native: మొదట అతను ఒప్పుకోలేదు, చివరికి సరే అన్నాడు.
sentences.roman: modaṭa atanu oppukōlēdu, chivariki sarē annāḍu.
sentences.en: At first he said no; in the end he said OK.

sentences.native: అసలు ఏం జరిగిందంటే, నా ఫోన్ ఇంట్లో మర్చిపోయా.
sentences.roman: asalu ēm jarigindaṇṭē, nā phōn iṇṭlō marchipōyā.
sentences.en: What actually happened is, I left my phone at home.

sentences.native: విషయం ఏంటంటే, రేపు నాకు సెలవు లేదు.
sentences.roman: viṣayam ēṇṭaṇṭē, rēpu nāku selavu lēdu.
sentences.en: The thing is, I don't have tomorrow off.
It's a long story, I'll tell you later.

tip.title: React out loud
tip.body:
- Telugu listeners react all the time: **ఊ**, **అవునా?**, **నిజంగా?**, **తర్వాత?**
- **అబ్బా** wow / ugh · **బాబోయ్** yikes · **అరే** hey! · **హమ్మయ్య** phew.
- Add **-ఆ?** to any word to echo it back in surprise: ఇంత **ధరా?** 'that much?', **నువ్వా?** 'you?'

sentences.en: Really? You got the job?
I'm telling you for real, it's not a joke.
Ugh, this heat!
Yikes, that expensive?
Hey, what are you doing here?

sentences.native: నీకేమైనా పిచ్చా? ఈ వర్షంలో బయటికి వెళ్తావా?
sentences.roman: nīkēmainā pichchā? ī varṣamlō bayaṭiki veḷtāvā?
sentences.en: Are you crazy? You're going out in this rain?
He's always cracking jokes.
Phew, we caught the bus.
Seriously? The exam is tomorrow?

tip.title: The girl I met: the clause comes first
tip.body:
- No 'who/which/that': the verb becomes a participle **before** the noun.
- Past **-ఇన**: నేను కలి**సిన** అమ్మాయి 'the girl I met'. Non-past **-ఏ**: వెళ్**ళే** బస్సు 'the bus that goes'.
- 'What you said': **-ది** on the participle: నువ్వు అన్**నది**, నేను చెప్**పేది**.

sentences.native: నిన్న నేను కలిసిన అమ్మాయి నీ ఫ్రెండా?
sentences.roman: ninna nēnu kalisina ammāyi nī phreṇḍā?
sentences.en: Is the girl I met yesterday your friend?
The restaurant you told me about has shut down.
This is the bus that goes to my office.
What he said is a lie.
Listen to what I’m saying.
Remember the thing we talked about yesterday?
Everyone asked about you.
Nobody listens to me.
You're coming tomorrow, right?
See? That's exactly what I'm saying!

tip.title: He said…: quote it, then అని
tip.body:
- Keep the speaker's own words, then **అని** + a verb of saying: వస్తా **అన్నాడు** 'he said he'd come'.
- Told someone to do it: stem + **-మని**: రమ్**మని** చెప్పింది 'she told me to come'.
- Apparently: **-అట** on the verb: రార**ట** 'apparently they aren't coming'.

sentences.en: Ravi said he'd come in five minutes.
Mum said to tell you to come for lunch.

tip.title: Little words that keep a chat moving
tip.body:
- **అంటే** I mean / so you mean · **మరి** so, and what about · **అసలు** actually, (not) at all.
- **అన్నట్టు** by the way (new topic) · **ఇంతకీ** so anyway (back to the point) · **ఏదేమైనా** anyway.
- **పోనీ** how about…? · **పోనీలే** never mind.

sentences.en: So you mean you're not coming?
So what did you do?
I never said that at all!
By the way, it's Sravani's birthday tomorrow.
So anyway, when are you coming?
Anyway, I'll call you tomorrow.
Well, how about meeting tomorrow then?
Never mind, it's no big deal.
Right, so where was I?
What else? Is everyone at home well?

lessons.title: Did you hear? Passing on news

tip.title: Gossip, Telugu style
tip.body:
- Pass it on with **-అట** 'apparently': పెళ్ళి కుదిరింది**ట** 'apparently the wedding's fixed'.
- Ask for more: **ఆ తర్వాత ఏమైంది?** · **గొడవ ఎందుకు?**
- Swear it's true: **ఒట్టు!** · Doubt it: **చెవిలో పువ్వు పెట్టకు!**
